name: Bounded Integer Sequence Encoding (BISE)
definition: BISE is an encoding technique used by ASTC to store numbers with fractional bits per character, packing information more efficiently than integer bit storage for arbitrary alphabet sizes up to 256 symbols.
summary: Bounded Integer Sequence Encoding is a variable-length coding method that minimizes storage waste for non-power-of-two alphabets by selecting optimal binary, trit, or quint packing schemes.
